newsitem.title: USA: Ill House passes contribution ban on gaming - papers.
newsitem.headline: Ill House passes contribution ban on gaming - papers.

text.p: The Illinois House approved a proposal to ban operators of casinos and horse-racing tracks from contributing to political campaigns, the Chicago Sun-Times and Chicago Tribune reported.

The ban would also extend to the operators, stockholders and directors of riverboats or racetracks from making contributions to political funds, a practice currently legal in Illinois, the Sun-Times reported.

The 70-42 vote to approve the ban came just two days after a government watchdog group reported in a study that gambling interests had contributed $696,627 to Illinois legislative leaders in the last six months of 1996 and more than $1.7 million in the last two years.
The bill now goes to the Illinois Senate, where it faces a tougher road, the Tribune reported.

Earlier this week, state Rep. Louis Lang, D-Skokie, withdrew a proposal to greatly expand gaming in Illinois to partly fund a state school construction bond program and provide about $800 million in property tax relief.
Lang said at the time he did not have the votes to pass the proposal through the House, but Gov. Jim Edgar also declined to support the proposal as written.
